newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bank notes 420 pct oversubscribed. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Egypt bank notes 420 pct oversubscribed. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]

text.p: A 150 million pound ($44.19 million) floating rate note offer by Egypt's private National Societe Generale Bank closed this week after it was oversubscribed by 420 percent, the bank said on Thursday.
Subscribers will receive 23.69 percent of their initial bid, a bank official said. The subscribers can pick up the excess money they paid from the bank's branches starting from Sunday.
The offer opened on June 17 and closed June 30.
The five-year, floating rate notes are in units of 1,000 pounds with a first coupon rate of 9.171 percent. The first coupon payment is September 30, the bank said in a newspaper announcement.
(Corrects to make clear rate is for first coupon payment, and corrects payment date).
The bank may redeem the notes after the first four years.

The bank forecast that its net profits would increase from its 57 million in 1996,to 65 million pounds in 1997, 75 million in 1998, 86 million in 1999, 99 million in 2000, 114 million in 2001, and 131 million in 2002.
